newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end mixed, March T-bond up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end mixed, March T-bond up.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended mixed in quiet trading, with March T-bonds recovering late to finish slightly higher.

But many technicians said March did not reject Friday's sell-off soundly enough to rekindle any near-term bullishness. And few players seemed willing to take a stand ahead of December inflation and retail sales data due on Thursday, some traders said.
"It was really a non-event," a Eurodollar futures trader said. He said most players were squaring up their positions after Friday's losses, some getting flat before Tuesday.

December consumer prices and retail sales will be released at 0730 CST/1330 GMT on Tuesday. Overall CPI was forecast up 0.3 percent and the core rate was seen up 0.2 percent, compared with up 0.3 percent and up 0.2 percent in the previous report.
Retail sales were forecast up 0.5 percent overall and up 0.4 percent excluding autos, versus an 0.4-percent drop in overall and an 0.3-percent gain ex-autos in the November report.
Heading into those data, March T-bonds posted an uninspiring day technically, traders said.

March climbed as high 110-22/32 early, but failed to challenge a key pivot at 110-28/32. That level is the 50-percent retracement of the September to December rally. Resistance at 111-00 and 111-4/32 also went untouched. One futures floor analyst said that until March makes a decisive move above 111-16/32, the mood is cautious at these levels.
Some traders said the idea that a Fed tightening may be at hand also kept a lid on the market.
"I think there's still some uncertainty, but the camps are filling up on the side of a tightening in February," another Eurodollar trader said.
He said strong data on Tuesday would solidify those perceptions.

At settlement, March T-bonds were up 2/32 to 110-13/32, T-notes were flat at 107-30/32, muni-bonds lost 2/32 to 114-8/32, T-bills were flat at 94.88, and June Eurodollars were flat at 94.13. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
